authorAbout.en: Junsang is a Korean teacher. In about two years he has taught around 100 students for more than 1,700 hours, mostly from Europe and the United States. He runs everykoreans.com, a website for learning Korean.

en: This is the second book of the series: the words ranked 1,001 to 2,000 by how often they appear in the TOPIK II word list we use on everykoreans.com, grouped by topic, so each unit mixes levels 3 to 6 and common and rare words. Book 1 has the 1,000 most frequent words. Each unit has 20 words, an example sentence for each, and short writing practice.
Read the table aloud, then cover the English and test yourself. Write your answers on the lines, check the answer key at the back, and come back a few days later.
You do not have to memorize 1,000 words in one go. One unit a day is a calm pace: 50 units, about seven weeks.

items.q: 이 마을은 맑은 물과 깨끗한 공기 덕분에 유명한 ___ 마을이 되었다.
items.en: This village became a famous longevity village thanks to clean water and air.

items.note: 長壽 longevity or living a long life (무병장수 long and healthy life) vs 將帥 military commander or general (용감한 장수 brave general). Different hanja roots sharing the same spelling.
기억력 (記憶力) is broad mental recall or retention (기억력이 좋다 good memory), whereas 암기력 (暗記力) is the specific skill of deliberately memorizing words or data (단어 암기력 skill at memorizing vocabulary).

기대다 covers both physical leaning (벽에 기대다 lean on a wall) and relying on someone (부모에게 기대다). 의지하다 is mostly about relying on a person or thing for support (부모에게 의지하다 rely on parents); for a physical lean it sounds formal or literary, so everyday speech uses 기대다.
촉촉하다 conveys pleasing, fresh, well-hydrated moisture (촉촉한 눈망울 moist glistening eyes). 축축하다 conveys uncomfortable, clammy, and unpleasantly soggy wetness (비에 젖어 축축한 양말 soggy wet socks).

items.note: 早期 early stage or period (암의 조기 진단 early diagnosis of cancer) vs native Korean fish yellow corvina (영광 조기 Yeonggwang corvina fish). Completely different origins.
新藥 newly developed medical drug (신약 개발 pharmaceutical development) vs 新約 New Testament biblical scriptures (신약 성서 New Testament). Two distinct Hanja terms.
차갑다 describes objective coldness of liquids or atmosphere (차가운 공기 cold air). 시리다 is piercing cold that causes bodily aches in hands, knees, or sensitive teeth (시린 손을 녹이다 warm aching cold hands).
Contrasting clinical blood procedures: 헌혈 (獻血) is donating blood voluntarily to save others (헌혈의 집 blood donation center), whereas 수혈 (輸血) is medically receiving blood (긴급 수혈 emergency transfusion).

치료 (治療) refers to clinical medical procedures, operations, or drugs to cure disease (병원 치료 hospital treatment). 치유 (治癒) focuses on natural or holistic emotional healing and recovery (자연 치유 natural healing).

items.note: Both mean symptoms, but 증상 (症狀) denotes specific bodily symptoms (기침 증상 cough symptom), while 증세 (症勢) describes the overall trend or severity of illness (증세가 호전되다 condition improves).

Pronounced the same ([집따]). 집다 means to pick something up with fingers or chopsticks (반찬을 집다 pick up a side dish). 짚다 means to lean on or press with a hand or stick (지팡이를 짚다 lean on a cane, 이마를 짚다 put a hand on one's forehead).
意識 cognitive consciousness or awareness (의식을 되찾다 regain consciousness) vs 儀式 formal ceremony or ritual (입학 의식 entrance ceremony). Two distinct Hanja terms.
負傷 physical injury or trauma (부상을 당하다 get injured) vs 浮上 floating to the surface or rising to prominence (새로운 문제로 부상 emerge as an issue). Unrelated Hanja terms.

보존 (保存) protects valuable heritage, natural ecosystems, or records from decay or ruin (생태계 보존). 유지 (維持) keeps an ongoing condition, habit, or standard stable over time (체중 유지 weight maintenance).
초대 (招待) is common invitation to personal events or meals (친구를 집에 초대하다). 초청 (招請) is highly formal invitation extended to dignitaries, experts, or state guests (해외 전문가 초청 inviting overseas experts).
숙이다 is tilting downward from the neck or waist (머리를 숙여 인사하다 bow). 굽히다 is flexing joints like knees and elbows (팔을 굽히다 bend arms) or figurative yielding of pride (자존심을 굽히다 swallow pride).
古典 time-honored classic book or piece of music (고전 소설 classic novel) vs 苦戰 hard struggle or uphill battle (원정 경기에서 고전하다 struggle in an away match). Different Hanja.

주최 (主催) refers to the sponsoring organization taking responsibility for an event (시청 주최 hosted by city hall). 개최 (開催) refers to the physical staging or opening of the gathering (행사 개최 staging an event).

items.note: 소중하다 (所重) emphasizes deeply cherished personal or sentimental value (소중한 가족 precious family). 귀중하다 (貴重) emphasizes objective rarity, utility, or high worth (귀중한 문화유산 valuable cultural heritage).
드러내다 is uncovering what was concealed or hidden from view (진실을 드러내다 reveal the truth). 나타내다 is expressing ideas symbolically or manifesting signs (기호로 나타내다 express in symbols).

Contrasting stances against adversity: 맞서다 is confronting hardship or opponents face-to-face (어려움에 당당히 맞서다 confront difficulties proudly), while 굴복하다 (屈服) is yielding or surrendering under pressure (위협에 굴복하다 yield to threats).

items.note: 安心 peace of mind or relief from anxiety (안심하고 쉬다 rest with peace of mind) vs 안심 tenderloin, a soft cut of beef or pork (소고기 안심 beef tenderloin). Same spelling, unrelated words.

기억 (記憶) is neutral cognitive storage of data or facts (비밀번호 기억 remembering passwords), whereas 추억 (追憶) specifically denotes nostalgic, emotionally cherished life moments (학창 시절의 추억 fond school memories).
눈길 gaze or glance (사람들의 눈길을 끌다 catch people's eyes) vs 눈길 snow-covered path or road (눈길 운전 driving on snowy roads). Two completely distinct words sharing spelling.

Opposite life intervals: 생전 (生前) refers to a person's living years before passing away (생전에 남긴 편지 letter left while alive), whereas 사후 (死後) refers to the period after death (사후 관리 posthumous arrangements).

items.note: 질투 (嫉妬) often arises in personal or romantic relationships fearing displacement (사랑에서 오는 질투). 시기 (猜忌) is cold envy directed toward another person's advantages or success (남의 성공을 시기하다 envy another's success).

items.q: 세상 물정에 어두운 ___처럼 행동하다가 사기를 당하기 십상이다.

items.note: 線 geometric line or wire (선을 긋다 draw a line) vs formal matchmaking meeting arranged for marriage (선을 보다 attend a marriage blind date). Distinct senses separated by context.

강사 (講師) refers broadly to course lecturers and instructors at academies, community centers, or colleges (학원 강사 academy instructor), while 교수 (敎授) is a faculty professor appointed at a university (대학교 교수 university professor).
꾸중 is formal scolding or reprimand from parents or superiors for a definite wrongdoing (선생님의 꾸중). 잔소리 is repetitive, tedious nagging over petty daily habits (청소하라는 잔소리 nagging to clean up).
Generational lineage opposites: 선조 (先祖) refers to ancestral predecessors from centuries past (선조의 묘소 ancestral graves), while 후손 (後孫) refers to future descendants (자랑스러운 후손 proud descendants).
Opposite temperaments: 조급하다 (躁急) is fretful and rashly impatient to rush outcomes (조급하게 서두르다 rush impatiently), while 느긋하다 is composed, leisurely, and patient (느긋한 주말 leisurely weekend).

items.note: 物價 market prices and cost of living goods (물가 상승 price rise) vs 물가 natural water's edge, shore, or riverbank (물가에서 놀다 play by the waterside). Unrelated word origins.
株式 financial stocks or corporate equities (주식 투자 stock investment) vs 主食 principal dietary staple food (밥은 한국인의 주식이다 rice is the staple food of Koreans). Completely distinct Hanja terms.
赤字 financial deficit or running in the red (무역 적자 trade deficit) vs 嫡子 direct legitimate heir in a family lineage (전통의 적자 legitimate successor of a tradition). Different Hanja roots.

수익 (收益) is income or returns an asset or activity brings in (임대 수익 rental income). 이익 (利益) stresses the profit left after costs, or a benefit in a broader sense (이익을 남기다 make a profit, 공공의 이익 public interest).

양성 (養成) focuses specifically on educating and qualifying individual specialists (전문 인력 양성). 육성 (育成) focuses on systematically promoting, subsidizing, and growing entire industries or sectors (벤처 기업 육성).

items.note: 제안 (提案) is putting forward a concrete proposal, initiative, or plan for mutual consideration (신제품 아이디어 제안), whereas 조언 (助言) is offering helpful advice to assist someone with guidance (선배의 따뜻한 조언 senior's warm advice).

추측 (推測) is deducing or guessing about an unverified current or past situation using clues (이유를 추측하다 deduce reasons), while 예상 (豫想) specifically projects future outcomes ahead of time (내일 날씨 예상 forecasting tomorrow's weather).

Both mean advice, but 조언 (助言) provides positive, supportive guidance to help (업무 조언 helpful work tips), while 충고 (忠告) offers direct, stern criticism to correct a mistake or fault (따끔한 충고 stern admonition).
報道 mass media journalism or press coverage (속보 보도 breaking news coverage) vs 步道 pedestrian sidewalk or paved footpath (보도를 걷다 walk along the sidewalk). Two distinct Hanja terms.
Opposites of justice: 정당하다 (正當) is ethically fair and legally justifiable (정당한 요구 rightful demand), while 부당하다 (不當) is abusive, unfair, and ungrounded (부당한 처벌 unjust punishment).
개정 (改正) is formal enactment of revised laws, treaties, or curriculum (교과서 개정). 수정 (修正) is localized editing or fixing errors in drafts or code (계획안의 부분 수정 minor edit of plan).

items.note: 求하다 seek, look for, or obtain (일자리를 구하다 search for a job) vs 救하다 save, rescue, or relieve from danger (위험에서 아이를 구하다 save a child). Two distinct Hanja verbs.
Both end in -서 (document), but 보고서 (報告書) reports completed findings or results (출장 보고서 business trip report), while 신청서 (申請書) applies for entry or approval (회원 신청서 application form).
고무 elastic rubber material (고무줄 rubber band) vs 鼓舞 psychological inspiration, uplift, or boosting of morale (사기 고무 inspiring morale, 고무적인 결과). Different origins.
Opposite employment market roles: 구직 (求職) is seeking a job as a candidate (구직자 job seeker), while 구인 (求人) is hiring and recruiting personnel as an employer (구인 공고 job opening notice).
Opposite mechanical operations: 조립 (組立) combines parts into a finished structure (부품 조립 parts assembly), while 해체 (解體) breaks a whole unit down into components (조직 해체 disbanding group).

items.note: 미루다 is common everyday Korean for putting off chores or decisions (결정을 내일로 미루다). 연기하다 (延期) is formal for officially rescheduling events or meetings (개막식을 다음 주로 연기하다).
課長 section chief or department manager in a workplace (인사과 과장 HR manager) vs 誇張 exaggeration or overstatement (과장된 표현 exaggerated expression). Different Hanja roots.
근무 (勤務) refers to serving active working hours or shifts at a specific post (근무 시간 work hours). 근로 (勤勞) refers broadly to economic labor as protected by law (근로 기준법 labor standards act).
Opposite durability terms: 임시 (臨時) is provisional and short-term (임시 직원 temporary staff), while 영구 (永久) is perpetual and lasting forever (영구 보존 permanent preservation).

items.note: 주의 (注意) is vigilance or care to avoid risks or errors (주의 사항 precautions). 주목 (注目) is focusing sight or public interest onto a prominent subject (전 세계의 주목 global spotlight).
방지 (防止) blocks an unwanted event or recurrent trouble from taking place (도난 방지 theft prevention). 예방 (豫防) takes prior health or safety precautions against future risks (독감 예방 flu vaccination).
事由 justified reason, cause, or pretext for an action (지각 사유 reason for being late) vs 私有 private personal ownership of assets or land (사유지 private land). Two distinct Hanja terms.

급여 (給與) is formal administrative terminology for all payroll compensation and benefits (급여 계좌 payroll account). 월급 (月給) is everyday conversational Korean for a monthly paycheck (이번 달 월급 this month's salary).

ko: 어릴 때부터 국어는 문법부터 배우는 어려운 과목이었고, 수능을 준비하면서는 더욱 어렵다고만 생각했습니다. 그런 제가 대학교에 다니던 중, 한국어 선생님을 하는 친구를 보고 "나도 한번 해 볼까" 하는 마음으로 도전하게 되었습니다.
처음에는 학생이 한 명도 없었습니다. 말 그대로 파리만 날렸습니다. 그러던 어느 날 제 계정으로 알림이 왔습니다. 한 학생이 수업을 예약했다는 소식이었습니다. 그때부터 가슴이 뛰기 시작했고, 그 학생을 위해 자료를 준비하는 일이 설렜습니다. 어쩌면 그때부터 한국어를 가르치는 일에 빠졌는지도 모르겠습니다.
재미로, 아르바이트처럼 시작한 일이 2년을 넘었습니다. 그동안 1,700시간이 넘게, 100명의 학생을 가르쳤습니다. 전 세계의 학생들을 만났고, 주로 유럽과 미국의 학생들을 가르쳤습니다.
가르치다 보면 설명이 안 돼서 답답할 만큼 아름다운 한국어를 만납니다. 그런 한국어를 가르칠 수 있다는 것이 저는 축복이라고 느낍니다. 지금은 한국어를 더 널리 알리기 위해 한국어를 가르치는 웹사이트 everykoreans.com 을 운영하고 있고, 대학교 공부도 함께 하고 있습니다.
en: I became a Korean teacher by accident.

Ever since I was a child, Korean class meant learning grammar first, and I thought of it as a hard subject, even more so while preparing for the national college entrance exam. While I was still in university, I saw a friend teaching Korean and thought, "Why not give it a try?"

At first I had no students at all. Truly, not a soul. Then one day a notification arrived on my account: a student had booked a lesson. My heart started to race, and I felt a thrill preparing materials for that student. Maybe that was the moment I fell for teaching Korean.

What began as a fun side job has now lasted more than two years. In that time I have taught over 1,700 hours to 100 students. I have taught students from all over the world, mostly from Europe and the United States.

When you teach Korean, you sometimes meet a beauty so deep that it frustrates you because you cannot explain it. I feel blessed to be able to teach that Korean. Today I run everykoreans.com, a website for learning Korean, to spread Korean further, and I am studying at university at the same time.
